subject: Soteria private cluster: architecture, node pools, and retention alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@soterialabs.com>, Soteria IT <it@soterialabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Soteria private deployment kickoff: baseline info request

Hi Oliver / Soteria IT team,

Thanks again for the call today. To make the first architecture pass and avoid surprises during the on-site sprint, could you please share the short inventory items below before our technical review next week? We've attached a one-page topology draft to help frame questions.

Quick asks (ideally as bullets in a reply):
- Rack-level network segmentation: are management, storage, and GPU traffic on separate VLANs? shared?
- Internet egress policy: outbound egress permitted, proxied, or strictly egress through firewall (include egress IPs if known).
- K8s control plane: do you provide a customer-managed control plane (bare-metal K8s) or want Redwood to run the control plane nodes?
- Desired model artifact retention and audit window (examples: 30d logs, 90d model artifacts, 7d KV cache).
- KMS/HSM: do you have an on-prem KMS or prefer Redwood-managed keys (we support customer KMS via API/HSM connectors).
- Preferred storage backend for long-lived model artifacts (NFS / Ceph/Rook / iSCSI / cloud-block via gateway).

Attachment: proposed-topology.pdf (simple rack + VLAN legend).

If you can attach the site diagram (rack map + switch uplinks) that will speed up the node placement recommendations.

Proposed next steps:
- You reply with the inventory items above (this thread)
- We create a first-pass nodepool + storage proposal and share a short decision matrix
- 60-min architecture review (video) the week of Jul 20th

Best,
Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0187
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@soterialabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soteria IT <it@soterialabs.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 14:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Soteria private deployment kickoff: baseline info request

Marissa — thanks, great to connect. Answers below and attaching the rack/switch diagram.

Inventory answers:
- VLANs: management and GPU traffic are on separate VLANs; storage traffic currently shares a VLAN with GPU traffic but we can carve it out if recommended.
- Egress: outbound is proxied via a perimeter firewall; limited outbound to specific destinations. We can provide allowed host/IP list.
- K8s control plane: we operate our own upstream Kubernetes (customer-managed).
- Retention goals: logs 90d, model artifacts (blobs) 180d, priority model versions pinned to 365d. KV cache is ephemeral — prefer 7d TTL.
- KMS/HSM: we have an on-prem HSM with a PKCS#11 interface; we'll provide connectivity during onboarding.
- Storage backend: currently running a Ceph cluster (Rook) for persistent block; also have an NFS cluster for shared home dirs.

Attachments: site-network-diagram.vsdx (rack and uplinks).

One more thing: we have a security questionnaire that will come through procurement — expect a few policy questions around data residency and audit logs.

Oliver
VP IT — Soteria Labs
oliver.grant@soterialabs.com | +44 20 7946 0XXX

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@soterialabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Soteria private deployment kickoff: baseline info request

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Oliver — this is exactly what we need. Based on your inventory and the fact you will manage the upstream K8s control plane and have Ceph/Rook, here's our initial, prioritized guidance (first-pass; we'll validate during the review):

Design summary (high level):
- Control plane: customer-managed K8s (you) — Redwood will deploy inference workers as namespaced deployments and operators. We'll run only inference pods/namespaced control components.
- Node pools:
  - infra-pool (small, x86): 3 nodes for Redis/metrics/ingress/sidecars (tolerations and taints for infra-only).
  - gpu-pool (A100/T4 equivalent): dedicated GPU nodes (autoscale via cluster-autoscaler) pinned to a GPU VLAN and isolated egress. Use local NVMe for token cache (ephemeral) + Ceph-backed PVs for model artifacts.
  - cpu-worker-pool (x86 large): for CPU-only model variants, batch preprocessing, and evaluation workers.
  - storage-proxy-pool (small): nodes with good network throughput for mounting Rook/Ceph and handling backups; run CSI controllers here if needed.

Storage & retention: 
- Model artifacts (immutable blobs): Ceph/RBD with replication factor >=2; mount via CSI. Enforce encryption at rest using your HSM-managed KMS keys (we support PKCS#11 connector).
- Ephemeral token/KV cache: local NVMe with node-level eviction (7d TTL as requested). We will configure prefix/KV cache to reduce egress to Ceph for hot models.
- Logs and audit: forward to your on-prem ELK/Graylog with 90d retention. Requests to enable request-level audit logging for 180d (to support compliance) will increase storage; we included this in the retention matrix.

Networking notes: 
- Keep GPU traffic on dedicated VLAN and L2/L3 isolation between storage and GPU VLANs to avoid noisy-neighbor saturation.
- Egress: because you have proxied egress, we'll provide a small set of destination IPs/domains (Redwood API endpoints for telemetry and package fetching) and a signed cert for mutual TLS where required.

Operational controls & SLOs: 
- Model promotions: support canary rollouts using a canary namespace + 10% traffic initially, then 50/50 for 24h.
- Autoscaling policy: conservative initial CPU/GPU scale thresholds; recommend manual burst window for training/reindexing.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Soteria: provide firewall egress IP allowlist and HSM access details (Oliver) — ETA: 2026-07-21
- Redwood (Karthik): produce nodepool YAML templates + CSI mount examples (nodepool-suggested.yaml) — ETA: 2026-07-19
- Soteria: confirm Ceph replication policy and usable storage from Rook (Emil/IT) — ETA: 2026-07-22
- All: 60-min live architecture review — propose Tue Jul 21 09:00 UTC / 11:00 CEST

Quoting Oliver's note for context:
> On Thu, 16 Jul 2026 14:05:00 +0200, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@soterialabs.com> wrote:
> VLANs: management and GPU traffic are on separate VLANs; storage traffic currently shares a VLAN with GPU traffic but we can carve it out if recommended.

Attached for the review: nodepool-suggested.yaml, retention-matrix.csv (short matrix mapping artifact type to retention and storage class).

Let us know if the Tue slot works and we will calendar-in.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
